Oh, no, it's not new at all. I remember being exactly like this way back in grade school, long before I had any of this pressure from work. My teachers always told my parents I was a bright kid, but I was just constantly misplacing my papers. Not really. I mean, I don't think I do things without thinking. I'm actually pretty careful, especially with my tools. You have to be, you know? No, I don't really have mood swings. I mean, my mood is pretty steady most days. I just wake up, get my coffee, and go to work. 

I have to have my coffee first thing, though. I use this old French press I found at a flea market years ago. I always try to read the magazines in waiting rooms, but they're always like three years out of date. Like, why am I reading about the 2019 summer Olympics in 2022? It just doesn't make sense to keep them around that long...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Mood swings? Yeah, no, I don't really have those. I'm pretty even-keeled.

No, I don't think so. I'm pretty good at rolling with the punches. In my line of work, you kind of have to be, because nothing ever goes the way you expect it to. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to just swap out a leaky faucet in this older house, built in maybe the 1950s. Simple job, right? Take off the old one, put on the new one. Nobody really smokes pipe tobacco anymore, do they? It's all just those little electronic things that smell like cotton candy...

I think it's just... how my brain is wired. Because I remember being exactly this way back in grade school, way, way before I ever had any of this job pressure. My teachers always told my parents I was a bright kid, but I was constantly misplacing my papers. 

My mom actually bought me one of those Trapper Keepers to try and help me stay organized. Do you remember those? They had that big Velcro flap that made that loud ripping sound every time you opened it in the middle of quiet reading time. I had one with a neon pink grid and a dolphin on it. I think it was Lisa Frank? Her stuff was everywhere back then. Everybody had the folders and the pencils. Pencils used to be so much better, honestly. The wood actually sharpened evenly. Now when you buy pencils, the lead is always broken all the way down the middle, so you sharpen it and the tip just falls right out. It drives me crazy at work when I'm trying to mark a measurement on a piece of drywall and my pencil tip just snaps off. And then you have to fish your utility knife out of your pocket to whittle it down because the sharpener is all the way out in the truck. Drywall dust gets absolutely everywhere, too, it just coats your boots and dries out your hands...

Oh, geez, sorry. I lost my train of thought again. Um, but yeah, back in school... my teachers said I'd just miss parts of the directions all the time, and they constantly had to come over and remind me to actually finish my classwork. So it's definitely not just the work environment. It's just always been me.

My grandmother used to have this huge Meyer lemon tree in her backyard down in Florida. The citrus bugs got to it eventually, though. Those little aphids just destroy everything if you don't spray neem oil on the leaves early enough in the season. \n\nNeem oil smells absolutely terrible, by the way. It's kind of like garlic and sulfur mixed together. I actually spilled a bottle of it in the trunk of my Chevy Nova back in '98, and I swear, no matter how much baking soda I dumped on the carpet, that car smelled like a rotten salad dressing factory until the day the transmission finally blew on the interstate. Getting towed off the highway is terrifying, the way the semis just blow right past you so fast the whole car shakes... \n\nWait, I'm sorry. Did you ask if I get irritated? No, I'm pretty easygoing, honestly. Small stuff is just small stuff.\n\nDoctor: Do you have mood swings?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really have mood swings. I mean, my mood is pretty steady most days. I just wake up, get my coffee, and go to work. \n\nI have to have my coffee first thing, though. I use this old French press I found at a flea market years ago. It's got this beautiful copper housing around the glass, but the plunger is a little bent, so if you don't push it down perfectly straight, the grounds shoot up the side and you end up drinking gritty coffee. There's nothing worse than getting a mouthful of coffee grounds when you're just trying to wake up. It reminds me of this time I had to fix a garbage disposal at this apartment complex over on 5th Street. The tenant had shoved, I kid you not, an entire bag of potting soil down the sink because they thought the disposal would just \"grind it up and wash it away.\" The whole P-trap was packed solid with dirt and perlite. Perlite is that little white stuff they put in potting soil to help with drainage, you know? It's actually a type of volcanic glass that expands when you heat it up, kind of like popcorn. I read about it once in this gardening magazine I found in a waiting room. I always try to read the magazines in waiting rooms, but they're always like three years out of date. Like, why am I reading about the 2019 summer Olympics in 2022? It just doesn't make sense to keep them around that long...\n\nWait, sorry. What were we talking about? Mood swings? Yeah, no, I don't really have those. I'm pretty even-keeled.\n\nDoctor: Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when something unexpected happens?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think so. I'm pretty good at rolling with the punches. In my line of work, you kind of have to be, because nothing ever goes the way you expect it to. \n\nLike yesterday, I was supposed to just swap out a leaky faucet in this older house, built in maybe the 1950s. Simple job, right? Take off the old one, put on the new one. But when I went to shut off the water under the sink, the shut-off valve—the original one from when the house was built—just crumbled in my hand. It was completely corroded. So suddenly, I've got water spraying everywhere, and I have to run out to the street to shut off the main water line. The water meter cover was stuck, of course, and I had to pry it up with a crowbar. I keep a really nice titanium crowbar in my truck for things like that. Titanium is great because it's so much lighter than steel, but it doesn't rust. I actually got it on sale at this little hardware store that was going out of business. It's so sad when those independent places close down. They always have the best stuff, and the people who work there actually know what they're talking about, unlike the big box stores where you ask a teenager where the PVC primer is and they look at you like you're speaking Greek. My grandfather used to run a hardware store in Ohio. He had these old wooden floors that would creak every time you walked down the aisles, and he smelled like sawdust and pipe tobacco. Nobody really smokes pipe tobacco anymore, do they? It's all just those little electronic things that smell like cotton candy...\n\nWait, I'm sorry. Did you ask about my emotions? No, I don't lose control or anything. I just deal with it. You have to, you know?\n\nDoctor: Do you find that your emotions often shift rapidly without an obvious reason?\n\nPatient: No, not really. My emotions don't just bounce around for no reason. I feel like there's always a cause, you know? Even if it's just being tired or hungry. \n\nSpeaking of being hungry, I've been trying to eat more protein lately. I read somewhere that it helps keep your energy levels stable throughout the day. I started buying these little packets of tuna, the ones that come in different flavors? The lemon pepper one is pretty good, but the jalapeño one is way too spicy for me. I don't know how people eat super spicy food. I had a roommate in my twenties who would put hot sauce on literally everything—eggs, pizza, even macaroni and cheese. She had this whole collection of hot sauces lined up on the kitchen counter. Some of the labels were hilarious, like \"Devil's Breath\" and stuff like that. She actually ended up moving to New Mexico, which makes sense because they put green chiles on everything out there. I visited her once, and the sky out there is just... it's so big and blue. It doesn't look real. We went to this alien museum in Roswell, which was kind of cheesy but fun. They had all these little green men statues everywhere. It takes a lot of arm strength to knead dough like that for hours. I tried making homemade bread once during the pandemic, like everybody else did, right? The sourdough starter thing. I named mine \"Doughlene\" like the Dolly Parton song. But I kept forgetting to feed it, and it just turned gray and smelled like old beer, so I had to throw it out. It's a shame because I love fresh sourdough. Especially toasted with a lot of butter. Real butter, not the margarine stuff. My mom used to buy margarine in these big plastic tubs, and she'd save the tubs to put leftovers in. So you'd open the fridge thinking you were getting butter, and it would be like, leftover spaghetti. It's funny how moms from that generation all did the same things. I mean, I don't think so? Like I said, I haven't really been to the doctor much. What does a comprehensive evaluation even look like? Is it like a bunch of tests or something? I've always hated tests. In high school, I used to freeze up whenever they handed out those Scantron sheets. The ones where you had to bubble in the answers with a number two pencil. If you didn't erase completely, the machine would mark it wrong. I always worried I wasn't bubbling it in dark enough. And the smell of those freshly printed test papers—like, the mimeograph ones? They always smelled so strongly of that weird ink. Some kids used to sniff the paper right when the teacher handed it out. 

Kids are so weird. My nephew is in middle school now, and he's obsessed with these little finger skateboards. Tech Decks, I think they're called? He'll just sit there at the dinner table trying to do kickflips over the salt shaker. Just easily annoyed by the radios and stuff.\n\nDoctor: Do you have trouble organizing your time or tasks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think I have trouble organizing things. I mean, I'm pretty good about keeping track of what I need to do. I use this heavy-duty aluminum clipboard for all my work orders. It's one of those contractor ones that opens up on a hinge so you can store extra paperwork and pens inside. I actually got it from a delivery driver who used to drop off plumbing fixtures at my old job. Frank, I think his name was. Or maybe Fred? No, Frank. \n\nHe drove this massive, ancient diesel box truck that smelled just awful, like burnt oil and French fries. He said he ran it on biodiesel he made himself in his garage. People do that, you know? They go to restaurants and ask for their used fryer oil. There's this diner near my house, Mama's Kitchen, they make the best curly fries, but their grease trap is an absolute nightmare to clean out. I had to snake their main drain once, and the amount of congealed grease was just... it was like concrete. You really need a high-pressure water jetter for that kind of blockage, but my boss at the time wouldn't authorize the rental fee for the equipment, so I was stuck out in the alley for six hours with just a manual auger. My arms were sore for a week after that. You really don't realize how much upper body strength you need for plumbing until you're fighting fifty feet of steel cable in the freezing rain... \n\nWait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my schedule or something? But yeah, no, I keep everything organized on my clipboard just fine.\n\nDoctor: Do you find it hard to calm down after something upsetting happens?\n\nPatient: No, not really. I mean, if something really bad happens, sure, it takes a minute, but I don't stay worked up forever. Like, I can usually just let it go and move on to the next thing. \n\nI try to just keep moving, you know? Like when I'm at the hardware store. I spend so much time at the hardware store, I swear I should just get a cot and sleep in aisle four. Aisle four is where they keep all the fasteners—screws, bolts, washers, all of it. But the way they organize it makes absolutely no sense. They have the metric bolts mixed in right next to the standard ones, and the little plastic baggies are always ripped open because people try to test-fit them and then just shove them back in the wrong bin. It drives me crazy. I was looking for a specific size toggle bolt last Tuesday for this drywall repair I was doing at a dental office. Dentists always have the weirdest lighting fixtures. They're these heavy, articulating arms that pull down over the chair, and if they aren't anchored straight into the stud, they just rip right out of the wall. Anyway, the dentist there, Dr. Evans, he has this massive saltwater fish tank in the waiting room. It's beautiful, really, with these bright blue tangs and clownfish. But saltwater tanks are a nightmare to maintain. The salt creep gets everywhere, it corrodes all the metal fittings, and the filtration systems are so loud if you don't pad the pumps right. I used to have a freshwater tank when I was a kid, just goldfish, mostly. They get huge if you put them in a big enough tank, though most people just keep them in those tiny little bowls where they can't even turn around...\n\nI'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. What was the question again? Something about being upset? But yeah, no, I calm down pretty quick. I don't hold onto things.\n\nDoctor: Do you find yourself getting easily irritated by small things that wouldn't normally bother you?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think so. Small things don't really get to me. Well, except maybe when painters just spray right over door hinges and strike plates instead of taping them off. That's just lazy, you know? \n\nI spent three hours on Tuesday trying to scrape layers of cheap gloss enamel off a strike plate in unit 4B. The tenant there, Mrs. Higgins, she's a sweetheart, though. She always bakes these little lemon bars whenever I come over to fix things. Lemon is actually my absolute favorite flavor for desserts. My grandmother used to have this huge Meyer lemon tree in her backyard down in Florida. The citrus bugs got to it eventually, though. Those little aphids just destroy everything if you don't spray neem oil on the leaves early enough in the season. \n\nNeem oil smells absolutely terrible, by the way. It's kind of like garlic and sulfur mixed together. I actually spilled a bottle of it in the trunk of my Chevy Nova back in '98, and I swear, no matter how much baking soda I dumped on the carpet, that car smelled like a rotten salad dressing factory until the day the transmission finally blew on the interstate. Getting towed off the highway is terrifying, the way the semis just blow right past you so fast the whole car shakes... \n\nWait, I'm sorry. Did you ask if I get irritated? No, I'm pretty easygoing, honestly. Small stuff is just small stuff.\n\nDoctor: Do you have mood swings?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really have mood swings. I mean, my mood is pretty steady most days. I just wake up, get my coffee, and go to work. \n\nI have to have my coffee first thing, though. I use this old French press I found at a flea market years ago. It's got this beautiful copper housing around the glass, but the plunger is a little bent, so if you don't push it down perfectly straight, the grounds shoot up the side and you end up drinking gritty coffee. There's nothing worse than getting a mouthful of coffee grounds when you're just trying to wake up. It reminds me of this time I had to fix a garbage disposal at this apartment complex over on 5th Street. The tenant had shoved, I kid you not, an entire bag of potting soil down the sink because they thought the disposal would just \"grind it up and wash it away.\" The whole P-trap was packed solid with dirt and perlite. Perlite is that little white stuff they put in potting soil to help with drainage, you know? It's actually a type of volcanic glass that expands when you heat it up, kind of like popcorn. I read about it once in this gardening magazine I found in a waiting room. I always try to read the magazines in waiting rooms, but they're always like three years out of date. Like, why am I reading about the 2019 summer Olympics in 2022? It just doesn't make sense to keep them around that long...\n\nWait, sorry. What were we talking about? Mood swings? Yeah, no, I don't really have those. I'm pretty even-keeled.\n\nDoctor: Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when something unexpected happens?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think so. I'm pretty good at rolling with the punches. In my line of work, you kind of have to be, because nothing ever goes the way you expect it to. \n\nLike yesterday, I was supposed to just swap out a leaky faucet in this older house, built in maybe the 1950s. Simple job, right? Take off the old one, put on the new one. But when I went to shut off the water under the sink, the shut-off valve—the original one from when the house was built—just crumbled in my hand. It was completely corroded. So suddenly, I've got water spraying everywhere, and I have to run out to the street to shut off the main water line. The water meter cover was stuck, of course, and I had to pry it up with a crowbar. I keep a really nice titanium crowbar in my truck for things like that. Titanium is great because it's so much lighter than steel, but it doesn't rust. I actually got it on sale at this little hardware store that was going out of business. It's so sad when those independent places close down. They always have the best stuff, and the people who work there actually know what they're talking about, unlike the big box stores where you ask a teenager where the PVC primer is and they look at you like you're speaking Greek. My grandfather used to run a hardware store in Ohio. He had these old wooden floors that would creak every time you walked down the aisles, and he smelled like sawdust and pipe tobacco. Nobody really smokes pipe tobacco anymore, do they? It's all just those little electronic things that smell like cotton candy...\n\nWait, I'm sorry. Did you ask about my emotions? No, I don't lose control or anything. I just deal with it. You have to, you know?\n\nDoctor: Do you find that your emotions often shift rapidly without an obvious reason?\n\nPatient: No, not really. My emotions don't just bounce around for no reason. I feel like there's always a cause, you know? Even if it's just being tired or hungry. \n\nSpeaking of being hungry, I've been trying to eat more protein lately. I read somewhere that it helps keep your energy levels stable throughout the day. I started buying these little packets of tuna, the ones that come in different flavors? The lemon pepper one is pretty good, but the jalapeño one is way too spicy for me. I don't know how people eat super spicy food. I had a roommate in my twenties who would put hot sauce on literally everything—eggs, pizza, even macaroni and cheese. She had this whole collection of hot sauces lined up on the kitchen counter. Some of the labels were hilarious, like \"Devil's Breath\" and stuff like that. She actually ended up moving to New Mexico, which makes sense because they put green chiles on everything out there. I visited her once, and the sky out there is just... it's so big and blue. It doesn't look real. We went to this alien museum in Roswell, which was kind of cheesy but fun. They had all these little green men statues everywhere. It's funny how we always picture aliens as little green men with big eyes. Why not purple or orange? I guess green just stuck in pop culture. \n\nWait, what was the question? Rapid shifts? Oh, no. I'm pretty steady. No sudden shifts out of nowhere.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your difficulties with paying attention and remembering things are affecting your relationships with friends and family?\n\nPatient: Well, with friends and family... I mean, they get frustrated with me sometimes when I forget to call back or zone out when they're talking. But honestly, the real problem is at work. It's turned into a serious issue lately. I've got this massive backlog of work orders I just can't seem to get through, and the tenants are starting to complain. \n\nThe property manager even had to put a safety review on my record because I left a ladder and some tools out in a hallway overnight. I just completely forgot they were there because I went to grab a specific drill bit from my truck and got sidetracked fixing the latch on the truck cap. Those caps are so finicky, especially the fiberglass ones. If the struts go bad, you're basically lifting a dead weight every time you open it. I replaced the struts on mine last winter. I ordered them online from this auto parts place that ships out of Michigan. My cousin lives in Michigan, up in the Upper Peninsula. Have you ever been up there? It's gorgeous, but the winters are absolutely brutal. They get \"lake effect\" snow, which means the cold air picks up moisture from the Great Lakes and just dumps feet of snow all at once. My cousin sent me a picture once where the snow was literally up to the roof of his garage. He has to use a roof rake to pull the snow off so the roof doesn't cave in. I can't even imagine having to do that. I hate being cold. That's why I always wear these insulated Carhartt overalls when I have to work outside in the winter. They're so stiff when you first buy them, you practically have to wash them ten times before you can bend your knees...\n\nOh, shoot, sorry. I'm doing it again. What was I saying? Right, work. Yeah, I'm really scared because I've been working toward this promotion to lead maintenance supervisor, and with the backlog and the safety review... I'm terrified this is going to cost me the promotion.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your difficulties with paying attention and remembering things are affecting your personal relationships outside of work?\n\nPatient: I mean, not really? Like I said, they get annoyed sometimes, but it's not like it's ruining my marriage or anything. My husband knows how I am. He just kind of sighs and repeats himself. It's one of those places where they make the pasta fresh right in front of you. You can see them kneading the dough through this big glass window. I named mine \"Doughlene\" like the Dolly Parton song. But I kept forgetting to feed it, and it just turned gray and smelled like old beer, so I had to throw it out. My mom used to buy margarine in these big plastic tubs, and she'd save the tubs to put leftovers in. I tried it once and just ended up flicking it straight into the mashed potatoes. Mashed potatoes are so hard to get out of things, especially if they dry. You have to soak the plates forever. I always tell the guys at work to rinse their dishes out in the breakroom sink, but they just leave them sitting there...\n\nAnyway, what was the question? A comprehensive evaluation? No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. Just the basic physicals for work.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you experience when you're trying to focus on a task, and how that affects your daily life?\n\nPatient: Well, it's like...
